title: Erdős #401: Factorial Divisibility with Prime Products

problemStatement.formal: ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℕ, (a₁! · a₂!) ∣ (n! · 2ⁿ·3ⁿ·...·pᵣⁿ) ∧ a₁ + a₂ > n + f(r)·log(n)
problemStatement.plain: Does there exist f(r) → ∞ such that for infinitely many n, there exist a₁, a₂ with a₁!·a₂! | n!·2ⁿ3ⁿ...pᵣⁿ and a₁ + a₂ > n + f(r)·log(n)?
whyMatters: Extends Erdős-Graham's classical factorial divisibility bounds
Tests whether extra prime power factors fundamentally change divisibility structure

proven: YES: Barreto-Leeham (2026) proved the conjecture using same technique as #729
Strong version FALSE: Sothanaphan showed 'for all large n' version fails via n = p_{r+1}^k - 1
Erdős-Graham baseline: without extra factors, a₁ + a₂ ≤ n + O(log n)
